four-fer power England to series win
 by Cricbuzz Staff •     Share Tweet Duckett brought up his hundred off 94 balls © Getty Duckett brought up his hundred off 94 balls © Getty Ben Duckett's seventh ODI century and Sonny Baker's four-wicket haul powered England to a 97-run victory over Australia in the series-deciding third ODI at Bellerive Oval, sealing a 2-1 series win. Duckett's 133 off 115 balls helped England post 328 before Baker's incisive new-ball spell left the hosts reeling at 34 for 3 in pursuit. Australia were eventually bowled out for 231 in 46.5 overs, with Matt Renshaw's 55 offering the only substantial resistance.
 Having been asked to bat, England made an aggressive start through Duckett and Tom Banton. The pair put on 74 for the opening wicket in 8.4 overs, with Banton, fresh off a century in Adelaide, taking the attack to Australia's new-ball bowlers to make 44 off 35 deliveries. Duckett, meanwhile, was relatively watchful early on before finding his rhythm, bringing up his half-century off 36 balls.
 Australia, without the services of Adam Zampa, who was ruled out with back spasms, turned to their makeshift spin options to rein in the scoring. Matt Renshaw proved particularly effective through the middle overs, dismissing Joe Root, Jordan Cox and eventually the centurion Duckett to finish with 3 for 51. Cooper Connolly and Travis Head also chipped in with a wicket apiece as England slipped against spin to go from 112 for 1 to 195 for 5.
 Duckett, however, had done enough to give the innings its backbone. He brought up his hundred off 94 deliveries and continued to score freely even as wickets fell around him. His knock finally ended in the 39th over when he top-edged Renshaw to Josh Inglis, having struck 15 fours and three sixes in his 115-ball 133.
 England needed a strong finish after losing momentum in the middle overs, and Will Jacks provided it. He struck 59 off 48 balls, adding useful partnerships off 56 and 44 with Duckett and Sam Curran respectively to take the visitors to 328. Jack Edwards was Australia's most successful bowler, returning figures of 4 for 31 in 5.3 overs.
 Australia's reply unravelled almost immediately. Gus Atkinson removed Travis Head for the third time in the series before Baker made an early impact at the other end. The young seamer dismissed Mitchell Marsh and Josh Inglis with deliveries that moved away, leaving Australia three down inside the first eight overs. Baker's early strikes left the hosts facing another uphill task in a run chase, having suffered a similar top-order collapse in Adelaide.
 Matt Renshaw and Alex Carey attempted to steady the innings, putting together 74 runs for the fourth wicket. England had opportunities to break the stand earlier, with Renshaw surviving two chances, but the left-hander made the most of his reprieves to bring up a half-century.
 Liam Dawson eventually ended the partnership, having Renshaw caught and bowled for 55 off 70 balls. Carey fell soon after, run out for 37 following a mix-up with Cameron Green. Green's own innings was cut short when he was struck on the helmet by a sharp Atkinson delivery and had to leave the field with a bloodied lip. He was subsequently replaced by concussion substitute Oliver Peake.
 Dawson then took charge of the middle overs, removing Connolly, Peake and Edwards to finish with 3 for 42. With Australia slipping to 203 for 9, the contest was effectively over, although the final wicket pair managed to delay the finish. Harry Brook eventually dismissed Spencer Johnson to wrap up the innings at 231, with a last-wicket stand having helped Australia avoid a second consecutive defeat by more than 100 runs. The victory completed an impressive turnaround for England, who were bundled out for 131 in Perth before responding with a 135-run win in Adelaide. A series win, even against a somewhat depleted Australian side, sets them up well for the big World Cup year in 2027.
 Brief scores: England 328 in 48.3 overs (Ben Duckett 133, Will Jacks 59; Jack Edwards 4-31, Matt Renshaw 3-51) beat Australia 231 in 46.5 overs (Matt Renshaw 55; Sonny Baker 4-45, Liam Dawson 3-42) by 97 runs.
